description: Implement milestone M1 of the hosted-service work: make the proxy safe and legible to run on a host you own and reach from your own machines. Scope is fixed by four specs under docs/specs/, each decomposing register entries from docs/saas-requirements.md into numbered, testable sub-requirements.

tech_stack.frontend: n/a — no UI in M1; the dashboard is M3
tech_stack.database: n/a — config is a JSON file until M2 (#4)
tech_stack.infrastructure: n/a for M1; the operator runs one process on their own host

architecture_decisions.decision: No runtime dependencies may be added
architecture_decisions.rationale: package.json declares dependencies:{} and the README states 'No dependencies. Node built-ins only.' (README:39). This is a product property, not an accident. Practically it means NFR-21.1's address classification is hand-written against node:net (isIP/isIPv4/isIPv6) rather than pulled from a library, and resolution uses node:dns promises lookup with all:true.

architecture_decisions.decision: Defaults derive from proxy.host rather than being independent switches
architecture_decisions.rationale: Bound to loopback the proxy keeps today's behaviour exactly, so existing local users see no change. Bound anywhere else every hardening switch defaults closed. An operator cannot reach the unsafe combination by omission, only deliberately. Applies to NFR-20.1, NFR-20.2 and FR-07.6.
alternatives_considered: Independent booleans defaulting closed everywhere (breaks local users)
Independent booleans defaulting open (fails open off-box)

architecture_decisions.decision: Address policy checks the resolved address and connects to it, not to the name
architecture_decisions.rationale: net.connect(port, host) (src/mitm.js:197) takes a hostname and resolves it itself, so resolve-check-connect-by-name resolves twice and a name can answer differently each time. Without NFR-21.2 the NFR-21.1 check is decorative. Blind-tunnelled traffic is spliced without TLS validation by the proxy (CON-09), so connecting by address costs nothing: the client's own handshake inside the tunnel still validates the certificate against the name it asked for.
alternatives_considered: Check the hostname only (defeated by DNS rebinding)

architecture_decisions.decision: Certificate files are placed during M1 enrolment although mTLS enforcement is M2
architecture_decisions.rationale: FR-16.1. Placing device.crt/key now means #6 does not have to redo enrolment. The files are inert until then.
alternatives_considered: Defer all certificate handling to M2 (forces a second enrolment change)

architecture_decisions.decision: Sequence tasks by file ownership rather than by dependency alone
architecture_decisions.rationale: The codebase is small and src/mitm.js and src/server.js are each touched by more than one spec. Two agents editing the same file in parallel is the failure the scope field exists to detect, so tasks that share a file are placed in different tiers even where their requirements are logically independent. In practice this forced task-5 behind task-4 (both own src/server.js) and made per-file test scopes necessary, since a shared test/ prefix reads as a collision.
alternatives_considered: Maximise parallelism and accept merge conflicts

architecture_decisions.decision: Internal seams shared by more than one task are contracted before implementation, like the wire format
architecture_decisions.rationale: API-first was applied to the error envelope because three tasks emit failures. The same reasoning holds for S1, S2 and S3, and was not applied until it was pointed out. A seam decided inside task-3 would be re-decided in task-4 and again in task-5.
alternatives_considered: Let task-3 establish the seams and have later tasks follow (concentrates risk in the largest task, already at 17 acceptance criteria)

tasks.title: Decide the three internal seams M1 tasks share
tasks.description: S1 destination resolution and policy (task-3), S2 request correlation (task-4, task-5), S3 enrolment module boundary (task-2). Each is shared by more than one task, so deciding them inside a task means the next task builds a second shape. This is the discipline already applied to the error envelope, turned inward. Each decision follows a pattern the codebase uses rather than introducing one: createEgressGuard for an injected policy collaborator, the existing ctx for request state, alias.js writing while claude-env.js stays pure.
acceptance_criteria: S1 — a destination policy collaborator with a classify(host, port) returning intercept, tunnel with the resolved address, or refuse with a reason that maps onto the error envelope; the lookup is injectable so a test can force a private address and answer differently on a second call

S2 — a correlation id generator, where it is created on the request path and on the CONNECT path, and how it reaches both the log line and the response message without changing the error envelope shape

S3 — enrolment owns the filesystem in a new module while claude-env.js stays pure; the settings merge is a separate pure function so FR-03.3 and FR-03.4 are testable without a filesystem; every path is a parameter with a default
Each decision cites the existing pattern it follows, with a file and line
What is deliberately not decided is listed with the task that owns it
tasks.test_approach_rationale: Interface signatures and placement decisions. There is no behaviour to assert -- the behaviour is asserted by the tasks that implement against them.
tasks.alternative_verification: Every decision names the existing pattern it follows with a file and line, and those citations are checked against the source. A task that finds a seam unusable amends this contract before diverging from it, rather than silently building something else.

tasks.title: Renew MITM certificates on age, not only on host mismatch
tasks.description: leafCovers() (src/mitm.js:54) checks the CA signature and the SANs and never reads the validity dates, so an expired leaf is reused rather than replaced and every intercepted TLS connection fails with no self-healing. Lifetimes at issuance are CA 3650 days (src/x509.js:141) and leaf 825 days (:151). Implement docs/specs/m1-certificates.md.
acceptance_criteria: NFR-17.1 — leafCovers rejects an expired leaf, and one whose remaining life is below the renewal threshold
NFR-17.2 — the same check applies to the CA certificate; a fresh leaf signed by an expired CA is replaced
NFR-17.3 — regeneration logs the reason: expired, near expiry, or host mismatch
NFR-17.4 — leafDays and renewBeforeDays are configurable under proxy.certs, with defaults shorter than today's 825
A leaf inside the window that covers the hosts is still reused — no needless churn
docs/configuration.md documents proxy.certs
tasks.test_approach_rationale: Pure date comparison driving a replace-or-reuse decision. createLeaf() takes days at issuance (src/x509.js:146) so a chain with a past notAfter can be minted directly — no clock manipulation, and a useful RED state is trivial.

tasks.title: Client enrolment writes both configuration locations
tasks.description: Nothing in src/ reads or writes ~/.claude/settings.json today; buildClaudeEnvLines (src/claude-env.js:33) emits shell exports only. Measured (F14-F17): shell env covers the pre-settings window, user-scope settings.json covers everything after including background agents, and project scope silently bypasses the proxy for background agents. Both are required. Implement docs/specs/m1-enrolment.md.
acceptance_criteria: FR-03.1 — writes to user-scope ~/.claude/settings.json; project scope is never used
FR-03.2 — also emits the shell export covering the pre-settings window
FR-03.3 — merges into an existing env block and preserves every unrelated key; the file is not rewritten wholesale
FR-03.4 — running enrolment twice produces byte-identical output
FR-03.5 — unenrol removes exactly what was added and leaves the machine reaching the upstream directly
FR-16.1 — places tenant-ca.pem, device.crt and device.key, private key owner-readable only
Tests use a fixture settings file carrying unrelated keys, not an empty object
tasks.test_approach_rationale: Merge, idempotence and reversibility are exactly the properties that break silently and are cheap to state as failing tests first. FR-03.4 and FR-03.5 are byte-comparison assertions.

tasks.title: CONNECT and forward policy: allowlist, address policy, fail-closed listener
tasks.description: The tunnel branch dials any host on any port with no filtering (src/mitm.js:175, :197), and relayHttpForward (src/server.js:247) is a second unrestricted path. connectAuthorized returns true when no proxy.apiKey is set (src/mitm.js:294), failing open. Implement docs/specs/m1-hardening.md. Emit refusals against docs/plans/contracts/m1-error-envelope.md.
acceptance_criteria: FR-07.1 — every destination is classified intercept, tunnel or refuse, defaulting to refuse
FR-07.2 — intercept applies only to the configured upstream host
FR-07.3 — tunnel applies only to an allowlist held as configuration data
FR-07.4 — a refusal answers 403 naming the host and opens no socket to it
FR-07.5 — the shipped allowlist is composed by running a client with it active; each entry records why it is there; what was refused during that run is recorded in the PR
FR-07.6 — the www.example.org intercept is removable, and off by default when proxy.host is not loopback
NFR-20.1 — a non-loopback proxy.host with no proxy.apiKey fails at startup naming the missing setting
NFR-20.2 — the loopback auth exemption is disableable, and off by default when proxy.host is not loopback
NFR-21.1 — a destination resolving to loopback, link-local or private is refused even when allowlisted
NFR-21.2 — the connection is made to the address that was checked, not to the name
NFR-21.3 — tunnelled destinations are restricted to port 443
NFR-21.4 — relayHttpForward enforces the same host and address policy
With proxy.host on loopback every current behaviour is unchanged
No runtime dependency is added; address classification uses node:net and node:dns
NFR-26 — the address tests exercise boundaries, not one member per class: the edges of 127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.169.254 itself, the 172.16-172.31 limits, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms
NFR-07 — an SSE response survives the new path; no idle timeout is introduced below the client watchdogs
NFR-06 — resolution does not add a DNS lookup per request; results are reused for the life of a tunnel at minimum, and the measured headroom (F07, F08) is not spent
tasks.test_approach_rationale: Security-relevant authorisation and destination decisions. NFR-21.2 in particular is only demonstrable by a test that makes a name answer differently on a second lookup, which forces the resolver seam to be designed rather than retrofitted.

tasks.title: Distinguish proxy-originated failures and document the way back
tasks.description: Three separate transport failures all report proxy_error / 'Upstream unreachable' (src/server.js:276, :551, :659) and a fourth reports 'Internal proxy error' (:489). Tolerable when the operator is the user; not once the proxy is elsewhere. The existing 403 handler (:745) is the model to extend. Implement docs/specs/m1-failure-modes.md against the error-envelope contract.
acceptance_criteria: FR-17.1 — each failure class produces a distinct error.type per the contract
FR-17.2 — an actionable failure names the concrete step, following the shape of src/server.js:745
FR-17.3 — a non-actionable failure carries an 8-hex correlation id in the message and the same id appears in the server log for that request
NFR-13.2 — unenrol is documented as the recovery step when the service is unreachable, and leaves a machine reaching the upstream directly
Existing 403, 429 and pin tests still pass unchanged
tasks.test_approach_rationale: Response classification is deterministic and asserted directly on the body. The correlation id's log correlation is likewise a direct assertion.

tasks.title: Detect a partially configured client
tasks.description: FR-18.1. ASM-13 records that nothing detects a half-configured machine: if one of the two configuration locations is lost, traffic leaks silently and everything appears to work. The detectable half uses a signal already on the wire — the pre-settings request arrives only when the shell export is present, so a session whose first contact is the post-settings burst was configured by settings.json alone.
acceptance_criteria: FR-18.1 — a session that first appears after settings load is reported as partially configured, naming the missing location
The report is visible without reading logs — activity stream or status endpoint
The inverse case (settings missing, shell present) is documented as not detectable proxy-side, with the reason
No false positive for a correctly enrolled client
tasks.test_approach_rationale: Detection is a function of the observed request sequence, which a test can feed directly. The undetectable inverse case is documentation, not code, and is carved out in the acceptance criteria.

tasks.title: Security review of the M1 boundary
tasks.description: Adversarial review of what M1 changed, against the threat that motivated it: an authenticated tenant using the operator's network position. Not a general audit — the boundary is the destination policy, the authorisation gate, and the certificate lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria: Attempts SSRF by name, by literal address, by redirect, and by a name that changes between resolution and connect; each is refused
Confirms no configuration reachable by omission leaves the listener open off-box
Confirms refusal messages leak nothing about the operator's internal network
Confirms the loopback path is unchanged for existing local users
Findings recorded with severity and a reproduction
NFR-27 — each finding carries a severity, becomes a failing test in the task that owns the behaviour, and no high finding is left open
tasks.test_approach_rationale: A review produces findings, not code. The behaviours it probes are already covered by the tests written in task-3 and task-5; adding a parallel suite here would duplicate them without adding assurance.
tasks.alternative_verification: Adversarial probing against a running instance, with each attempt and its outcome recorded in .agents/results/result-qa.md. Anything that gets through becomes a failing test in the owning task before the finding is closed. A high-severity finding blocks M1 from closing (NFR-27).

tasks.title: Bring the documentation in line with what M1 shipped
tasks.description: M1 changes the configuration surface, the failure messages, and how a client is set up. docs/configuration.md, docs/proxy-modes.md and docs/usage.md all describe the current behaviour and will be wrong in places.
acceptance_criteria: proxy.connect and proxy.certs documented in docs/configuration.md alongside the existing keys
docs/proxy-modes.md no longer claims arbitrary hosts are blind-tunnelled
Enrolment and unenrol documented, with unenrol named as the recovery step when the service is unreachable
docs/specs/ requirement IDs still resolve to what was built; any divergence is corrected in the spec, not silently in the code
No documentation references a file, flag or config key that does not exist
tasks.test_approach_rationale: Prose. There is no behaviour to assert.
tasks.alternative_verification: Every config key, file path and command named in the changed pages is checked against the source; the check is recorded in the PR description.

fields.allow: string[] — hostnames permitted to blind-tunnel; the upstream host is implicit and not listed
fields.allowPrivateAddresses: boolean — default false when proxy.host is not loopback
fields.allowLoopbackClients: boolean — default false when proxy.host is not loopback
fields.testHost: boolean — default false when proxy.host is not loopback

fields.leafDays: number — leaf lifetime, default shorter than today's 825
fields.renewBeforeDays: number — renew this far ahead of expiry

security: NFR-20 — authenticate every non-loopback client; fail closed when no credential is configured
NFR-21 — constrain where the proxy may open a connection, checking the resolved address and connecting to it
No runtime dependency may be added; the address classifier is written against node:net
NFR-26 — boundary coverage where a requirement classifies a range
NFR-27 — findings carry severity and gate the milestone
performance: NFR-06 — the edge adds no measurable latency; measured at 5.00s vs 5.01s direct (F07, F08). Address resolution adds one lookup per CONNECT and must not be per-request when cacheable
scalability: Out of scope for M1 — one operator, own accounts. Tenant fair-share is #23 in M4

testing_strategy.unit_tests: node --test, the repository's existing harness. Each spec's §5 table maps requirement to test one-to-one; those tables are the acceptance criteria. NFR-26 requires boundary values wherever a requirement sorts inputs into classes; the address policy in task-3 is the case that matters.
testing_strategy.integration_tests: task-3 needs a resolver seam so a test can force a name to a private address and make it answer differently on a second lookup. That seam is what makes NFR-21.2 implementable at all.
testing_strategy.e2e_tests: FR-07.5 is discharged by running a real client with the allowlist active and recording what was refused. It is a validation activity, not a unit test, and has no row in any spec test table. Defect handling follows NFR-27: severity, a failing test in the owning task, and no open high finding at milestone close.
testing_strategy.performance_tests: None for M1. The latency claim is already measured (F07, F08).

stakeholders_identified: operator (the account owner, and the only M1 user)
future tenants — out of scope until M2

top_risks: RSK-03 — a client release moves the behaviour this design rests on (H/H); F03 and F06 each caught it moving
RSK-04 — the upstream response contract changes and quota tracking degrades silently (M/H); UNTREATED, and nothing watches for it
RSK-02 — the allowlist refuses a host a real session needs (M/M); composed from -p and --bg observations only
RSK-07 — an operator deliberately opens a hardening switch (L/M); defaults guard omission, not intent
RSK-01 — limits key on the egress IP, so pooling yields no multiple (M/H); observable once M1 runs
treatments: RSK-03 — NFR-10 canary before adopting a release as the floor; NFR-22 isolates the tracking code
RSK-04 — none in M1. Closing it means building the watch, which belongs with the canary in #16
RSK-02 — FR-07.5 composes the allowlist by running a client and recording refusals
RSK-07 — defaults derive from proxy.host so the unsafe state needs intent (NFR-20)
RSK-01 — egress.pin and sx.mode already exist; residual is metered bandwidth against donations (CON-08)
iso_31000.register: docs/saas-requirements.md §10 — RSK-01 … RSK-08, rated with owner and residual

approval_required_for: The composed allowlist (FR-07.5) — it decides what a client can still reach
Shortened certificate defaults (NFR-17.4) — renewal cadence is operator-visible
Any deviation from a spec requirement; the spec is corrected first, not the code silently
